description: Somos un equipo apasionado por la ciencia, la tecnología y la innovación, enfocado en transformar ideas en soluciones para problemas reales. Buscamos personas creativas, comprometidas y con iniciativa, interesadas en la programación, inteligencia artificial, investigación y desarrollo de proyectos. Valoramos el trabajo colaborativo, el pensamiento crítico y las ganas de aprender para generar un impacto positivo.
summary: TerraNova Vision is an AI-powered environmental monitoring web platform developed to study vegetation dynamics and water-stress conditions across Mexico. Built with a Python, PyTorch, and FastAPI backend (ia-local) and a Next.js and React frontend (migracion node), the system integrates NASA MODIS (MOD13Q1 V061) satellite data, NASA POWER meteorological variables, and NOAA’s ONI index into a unified geospatial database.   To address the "Be an Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge, TerraNova Vision transforms large Earth science datasets into accessible, interactive maps and time-series projections. It combines statistical trend analysis—using the Mann-Kendall test, Sen’s slope, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction—with predictive models (VegForecaster, built on a Transformer architecture, and RegimeForecaster) to identify what is changing, where it is occurring, its magnitude, and its statistical significance.  This solution is important because it separates sustained regreening or degradation trends from short-term natural fluctuations. By making satellite and climate analytics accessible to students, researchers, and institutions, it supports proactive ecosystem monitoring and drought-condition assessment.
details:
What It Does & How It Works TerraNova Vision is an environmental monitoring web platform that integrates satellite remote sensing, climate variables, statistical trend analysis, and artificial intelligence to study vegetation dynamics and detect water-stress conditions. Designed to systematically determine what is changing, where it is occurring, its magnitude, and whether the variation is statistically significant, the platform operates through a structured workflow:

  • Data Acquisition & Exploration: Preliminary data exploration is supported by NASA Giovanni, while core datasets include 16-day, 250-meter spatial resolution vegetation indices (NDVI, EVI, and VCI) from NASA’s MODIS MOD13Q1 V061 product, meteorological variables from NASA POWER, NOAA’s Oceanic Niño Index (ONI), and CMIP6/SSP climate scenarios.
  • Geospatial Processing & Statistical Analysis: Datasets are cleaned, standardized, and organized into a geospatial database. To separate sustained environmental trends from temporary fluctuations, the system applies the non-parametric Mann-Kendall test, calculates rates of change using Sen’s slope, and controls false positives across millions of pixels via the Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction.
  • AI Forecasting & Visualization: Two deep learning models—VegForecaster (built on a Transformer architecture with attention mechanisms) and RegimeForecaster—analyze historical patterns and estimate future vegetation behavior. In our national analysis of Mexico (2,271,726 pixels from 2020–2025), TerraNova Vision identified statistically significant trends across 24.82% of the area (21.86% regreening and 2.96% degradation), while VegForecaster achieved an R² of 0.9255 in blind 2024–2026 evaluations.

Benefits & Intended Impact TerraNova Vision transforms massive, complex Earth science datasets into interactive maps and time-series visualizations that non-specialist users can easily interpret. Its intended impact is to democratize access to geospatial and climate analytics for students, researchers, and environmental institutions—supporting proactive ecosystem monitoring, early drought and water-stress detection, and evidence-based environmental decision-making.

Tools, Coding Languages & Technologies The system is built on a modular architecture split into two primary components:

  • Backend (ia-local): Developed in Python, utilizing PyTorch for deep learning models, FastAPI for backend services, and pandas and xarray for processing CSV and NetCDF geospatial datasets.
  • Frontend (migracion node): Built with Next.js and React to provide an interactive web interface for exploring geographic maps, historical trends, and projections.
  • Scientific Platforms & Data Sources: NASA Giovanni (GES DISC), NASA MODIS (MOD13Q1 V061), NASA POWER, NOAA Climate Indices (ONI), and CMIP6/SSP models.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

  • Creativity: TerraNova Vision bridges classical non-parametric geostatistics (Mann-Kendall, Sen’s slope, and FDR correction) with modern Transformer-based time-series forecasting, linking spectral vegetation indices directly with macro-climatic oscillations (ENSO/ONI) inside an accessible web platform.
  • Factors Considered: Our team accounted for seasonal and non-linear variable behaviors so that short-term natural variability—such as El Niño and La Niña events—is not mistaken for permanent trends. We also prioritized scientific rigor and transparency by validating models against independent blind test periods, reporting calibrated uncertainty intervals, and clearly distinguishing historical satellite analyses in Mexico from heuristic projections available for the United States and Canada.
